title: A Workflow Roofline Model for End-to-End Workflow Performance Analysis
problem: Understanding end-to-end performance of scientific workflows on HPC systems is challenging as next-generation instruments produce data at higher resolutions and faster rates. Workflows exhibit diverse performance bottlenecks ranging from system bandwidth constraints to node-local performance to CPU preprocessing limitations.
motivation: Modern experimental instruments require performance analysis methodologies to meet productivity goals for high-quality scientific throughput on HPC systems.
method: The paper introduces a Workflow Roofline model connecting workflow end-to-end performance to peak node and system performance constraints. Four diverse workflows are analyzed: LCLS (bandwidth-bound), BerkeleyGW (node-performance-bound), CosmoFlow (CPU-preprocessing-bound), and GPTune (data-control-flow-bound). The methodology characterizes bottlenecks by comparing workflow execution characteristics against roofline constraints at system and node levels.
key_novelty: Extending the classical Roofline performance model to end-to-end workflow analysis enables comprehensive bottleneck identification and performance characterization across heterogeneous workflow patterns.
contributions: Workflow Roofline model for end-to-end workflow performance analysis on HPC systems
Characterization and identification of diverse performance bottleneck types across workflow classes
Demonstration across four representative workflows spanning experimental, traditional HPC, AI, and auto-tuning domains
Framework for motivating and guiding workflow optimizations

metrics.other: Performance bottleneck characterization relative to peak system and node performance

limitations: Limitations and applicability boundaries are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Workflow-level performance modeling and bottleneck analysis
